# Weeks on Fire — full agent brief

This file is a dense, crawlable summary of the project for AI agents and research tools.
Prefer linking the live site and GitHub paths when citing.

## Identity

- **Name**: Weeks on Fire (`weeks_on_fire`)
- **Type**: Short-film series + open production hub
- **Live site**: https://ford442.github.io/weeks_on_fire/
- **Repository**: https://github.com/ford442/weeks_on_fire
- **Author**: ford442
- **Tools**: Grok Imagine / xAI (visuals), Minimax Music (audio), React + Vite + Tailwind (hub UI)
- **License / access**: Public GitHub repository; free to browse and reference

## Elevator pitch

Weeks on Fire is a personal short-film series that intercuts narrative scenes with musical cutaways. Still images and video frames are generated with Grok Imagine; soundtrack cues are authored as Minimax Music style prompts (and sometimes full lyrics). The GitHub repo is the production archive (markdown synopses, screenplays, SRT placeholders, prompts). The deployed Vite app is a cinematic production hub with seven views: Visual Archive, Timeline, Songs, Daisy Bell, Suggestions, Characters, and Crew.

## Site structure (client SPA)

The hub is a single-page app. Views are toggled in-app:

1. **Visual Archive** (Grok Imagine Archive) — Production stills, cutaway suggestion prompts, and test ideas — scene, suggestion, test, and character lanes with copy-ready Grok prompts.
2. **Timeline** (Production Timeline) — Track scene creation, prompt evolution, media links, and status. Export JSON to commit production history.
3. **Songs** (Minimax Music Catalog) — Browse the series soundtrack — Minimax style prompts, lyrics, episode ties, and copy-ready generation notes.
4. **Daisy Bell** (Daisy Bell Cutaway) — Rubella & Lillith on the flower bicycle into old London — color HD keyframes beside intentional scratchy period film, sequence board, and street sights.
5. **Suggestions** (Suggested Cutaways) — Every current cutaway, one-panel gag, and scene suggestion — timed segments with copyable Grok Imagine / Gemini Omni prompts.
6. **Characters** (Character Bible) — Recurring cast and lawn-ensemble roles — including Qing Rao (清饶), the crystal-skull keeper on the Episode 03 Monster Mash lawn.
7. **Crew** (Series Crew) — Meet the fictional writer, producer, director, and crew behind Weeks on Fire — bios, quotes, and series credits.

Crawlers that do not execute JavaScript still receive a content-rich HTML shell (title, description, Open Graph, JSON-LD `TVSeries`, and static lists of scenes/songs/episodes inside `#root`).

## Character bible

- **Lillith Vale** — The Instigator — black-lace cabaret energy
- **Rubella Vale** — The Witness — lead singer & hologram bait
- **Qing Rao** — Crystal-skull keeper — elegant lawn observer
- **Justine** — Deadpan finisher — fourth core lawn cast
- **Madelin** — Manic bag lady — skull-tote chaos agent
- **Scarlet** — Silent third sister — sidewalk lecture flank
- **The Pizza Guy** — Running anchor of mundane persistence
- **Riley Smith** — The stranger on the center line — unemployed technician with good data
- **Kenji “Shred” Sato** — Glam-Sham-Poo brand ambassador / alumnus

## Cutaways & suggestions

- **911 for the Wrong Shade of Blue** (911-wrong-shade) — Karen reports existential zoning. Operator asks if anyone is bleeding. “Democracy is bleeding, Steven.” Transfer loop until pizza arrives.
- **Cat POV** (cat-pov) — No dialog. The Episode 3 black cat walks Halloween, watches the laser lawn, clocks the Pizza Guy from ankle height, and is still on the driveway when the purple light becomes décor.
- **Choose Your Basalt** (choose-your-basalt) — Dead-pan educational cabaret duet: Lillith and Rubella classify lava types in their gothic living room, then the floor opens onto magma. Ends with “That’s nature for us” / “Science.” before a Twilight Time trance smash-cut.
- **Empty Highway Confession** (empty-highway-confession) — 4:17 a.m. The driver talks to the radio. Billboard: KEEP GOING. No advertiser.
- **EyeWash Station Idents** (eyewash-idents) — Six analog bumpers: Please Stand By, Rinse Cycle, Unscheduled Programming, Aspect Ratio Matters, We Always Return, 3:44 Again. One still, one sting, one Continuity Voice line each. Nobody comments on the frame.
- **Cities in the Shell** (gag-cities-in-the-shell) — 2 a.m. oyster bar; each opened shell holds a tiny lit city; she squeezes lemon over one and sets it aside. Tonight's selection is a little metropolitan. Vivienne.
- **Closed for Cosmic Reasons** (gag-closed-for-cosmic-reasons) — Night infinity pool; laminated sign; the water hovers three feet up, still reflecting the city. She sits dry underneath and uses it as a ceiling. Vivienne energy.
- **Complaint Window, Deep Field** (gag-complaint-window-deep-field) — A wood-and-brass service window floating in a Hubble field; she slides a triplicate form; stamp: DENIED; now serving: —. Liliane files.
- **Furnace Season** (gag-furnace-season) — Foundry gala; molten iron as the room's weather; she warms her hands at the pour; sparks die on mink. Vivienne hired a climate.
- **The Ice That Exhales** (gag-the-ice-that-exhales) — Banquet ice sculpture of a woman melting into cigarette smoke, not water; cloth dry; waiter adjusts her a quarter inch. The Two as ice and absence.
- **The Moon Is Collect** (gag-the-moon-is-collect) — Red rotary, taut cord to a huge moon, empty chair, abandoned gloves. Someone is calling collect; the charges are astronomical; she stepped out. Liliane energy.
- **The Overnight Conservator** (gag-the-overnight-conservator) — 3 a.m. gallery; she dusts a kouros; it holds her champagne; she holds its broken forearm like a clipboard. Post-gala Two. Sibling hour to Master Control.
- **Third Shift Porcelain** (gag-third-shift-porcelain) — Couture mannequins at a factory time-clock; one smokes chrome in the dock door. Beauty is hourly; overtime is not discussed. The Two do not punch out.
- **Gallery Fog / Caffeinated Melon** (gallery-fog) — Espresso-hooked melon emits honesty fog. Ninety seconds of truth. Then everyone pretends. Justine eats crackers.
- **Home Sweet Void** (home-sweet-void) — After the cockpit cruise they are inside. Greeting is the jumbo Earth marshmallow bag on the glass table. Conversation (space speeding) starts before the floor. White asteroid-ride worms sneak the baseboard, sit up as a cut, and hog the scene. The white building cat speaks once and is stopped by glow, not a beam. Daisy, Hanshaw, and the bird joke remain this week's musical spine — this packet waits its turn for Imagine generation.
- **We Play to Win (House of Mirrors Rally)** (house-of-mirrors-rally) — Vivienne and Liliane play ping-pong in a ruined ballroom. Plaster falls. They do not flinch. Pizza box on the intact half of the table.
- **Item Three: Decorative Accent** (item-three-decorative-accent) — Emergency HOA meeting. The purple driveway light is tabled as a decorative accent. Brad has swatches. Biscuit steals the gavel. Pizza Guy at the door.
- **2AM Laundromat Slow Dance** (laundromat-slow-dance) — Two unnamed strangers fold a sheet, then slow-dance between dryers. The attendant mops around them. EyeWash always on in the corner.
- **Marble Tick Tack: Wrong Sets** (marble-tick-tack-worlds) — Sibling of the night-lot take on the same instrumental. Magnets never notice while a generating intelligence swaps the episode: horseshoe cabinet, Halbach desert, hopping mountain lion in the woods, Meissner ice, Helmholtz saucer, London maglev under a flower tandem, Seoul non-contact gears, ferrofluid smash, souvenir fridge magnets chaining home. Station objects hop; magnets travel. Roley Voss grammar, jokier sets.
- **Marble Tick Tack** (marble-tick-tack) — Pure animation bridge at 136 BPM. No faces. Cabinet marble chorus walks one night lot: doorway onto a dirt alley where spheres jump a visible gap to slam together and then gear without touching around a copper Rodin torus, then an unreal green lawn whose three coils fire a rotating field while a dumbbell rod pair tumbles end-over-end and the magnet tower stands on the 68 BPM kick and slumps in the gap, then frozen ferrofluid rain at the dirt/grass seam — a bound pair in mutual orbit rolls home and jumps the last gap into a Gauss chain on the same shelf. Cylinders spin on their ends and precess; the rooms vibrate on the eighths. Dancers hop, magnets orbit. Roley Voss lane.
- **Master Control, 4 AM** (master-control-4am) — Oz logs a timecode. One monitor shows this room a few seconds ahead. He stands up to get coffee. He does not look at the monitor. “It's not haunted, it's unscheduled.”
- **Molten Silver Sphere** (molten-silver-sphere) — Pure visual cutaway: a glossy molten silver liquid-metal sphere hovers in a pitch-black cave, pulsating to an unseen deep beat while cavern walls snap between high-contrast checkerboard and electric neon line grids. Three maxed-detail video prompt variations — slow zoom, orbital neon veins, and macro chromium dive.
- **Monster Mash Finale** (monster-mash-finale) — Rubella covers "The Monster Mash" on the post-snake-battle lawn while a cursed monster party erupts — Nixon, Furbies, knife-kittens, Skeksis and more. Amy and Alec return from the hiking sketch in full costume to dance, a Thriller-style werewolf moonwalks the perimeter, Lillith runs a parallel spy heist, and the hologram reveal tips into a Spy vs. Spy noir outro.
- **Morning After the Portal** (morning-after-the-portal) — Golden-hour cul-de-sac cleanup. Someone power-washes a sigil. Pizza Guy now delivering breakfast burritos.
- **Mountain Lion Wildflower Field** (mountain-lion-wildflowers) — POV leash: a mountain lion insists on showing us a field. Flowers escalate into botanical surrealism, then give way to open ocean and come back bigger and stranger on the far shore. Arrival: a sunlit clearing already full of other mountain lions. Two Minimax beds at 110 BPM — the ocean crossing IS the crossfade from Come Further into Here They Are. No swimming, no peril. Do not run 2 minutes of drag.
- **Article Seven** (mv-article-seven) — Mandatory funk interval. Plastic steward reads the laminated card. Remaining time is always fourteen minutes. The lawn is on break.
- **Call Forty-Seven** (mv-call-forty-seven) — Karen reports existential zoning. Each transfer adds a bar of hold music. Democracy is bleeding, Steven. The call never drops.
- **Closed Since Ninety-Eight** (mv-closed-since-ninety-eight) — Two reflections leave a house of mirrors in the wrong car. The radio is a station that signed off in 1998. Harmony is always one bar late.
- **Empty Parking Lot Waltz** (mv-empty-parking-lot-waltz) — Last two people in a vast wet lot. They could go or they could stay. The last chord never arrives.
- **Haunted or Unscheduled** (mv-haunted-or-unscheduled) — Master Control 4 AM underscore — Rhodes four-note loop that never develops, 3:44 twice identically, program bleed on the second pass. Not a second sign-off.
- **Heart Rate Optimal** (mv-heart-rate-optimal) — A heart-rate alert that thinks it is a ballad. 78 and 78. The chorus would like to go to ninety; the watch does not approve.
- **Heels or No Entry** (mv-heels-or-no-entry) — A rooftop bouncer recites the door policy while the skyline burns. She produces emergency stilettos. The kick arrives after Approved.
- **Neon Exit Sign** (mv-neon-exit-sign) — Series signature. Wet alley of EXIT signs that never lead outside. The Two only as reflections. Don't smudge the mascara.
- **Pepperoni or Margherita** (mv-pepperoni-or-margherita) — Fifteen seconds of cheerful ad, hard cut, then a deadpan ballad about arriving when chaos peaks.
- **Porch Light Meridian** (mv-porch-light-meridian) — Crane up from a porch bulb after chaos. The yard is small but the sky will not fit.
- **Quarter to Seventy-Five** (mv-quarter-to-seventy-five) — No chorus — only the title phrase, a clock stuck at 3:44, and an FM needle drifting left.
- **Receipt Dated Thursday** (mv-receipt-dated-thursday) — Continuity Voice reads a poodle’s return receipt from a store that will not exist until Thursday. The barcode is always one digit short.
- **Rinse Cycle** (mv-rinse-cycle) — Sign-off theme. Comfort that curdles on the second pass. Nine-bar phrases, late resolutions.
- **Static Between Stations** (mv-static-between-stations) — The dial left between two songs on purpose. Dashboard glow, mercury streetlamps, laundromat fluorescents humming with the hiss.
- **Strange Light** (mv-strange-light) — Sun and moon sharing one daylight sky. One witness. Quiet cosmic lawbreaking. Complements the Episode 3 crane.
- **The Laundromat Saints** (mv-the-laundromat-saints) — Two strangers alternate lines like strangers who accidentally agree. Dryer thumps on bar 5. Diegetic EyeWash TV, then full score for the slow dance.
- **The Most Refreshing Drink** (mv-the-most-refreshing-drink) — EyeWash sponsor for an over-engineered glass of ice water. Apparatus clicks in the dark lab; the gulp lands a beat before the ice. No sung lead.
- **The Roof Knows How to Wait** (mv-the-roof-knows-how-to-wait) — Rubella inventories a ceiling that has not fallen yet. Natural ventilation. The extra bar is the plaster still deciding.
- **This Program Contains Dialogue** (mv-this-program-contains-dialogue) — Pre-program warning sung as a hymn. S&P will not stamp until someone talks. The card never changes.
- **Ultra Screech (Glam-Sham-Poo)** (mv-ultra-screech) — Joke TV commercial for Ultra Screech Formula, conformed to the 2:51 Ultra Screech 2 bed with the take-1 scream spliced on. Cold-open scream, Kenji hype, laundry-room dual frontwomen, salaryman panic, product bottle, HOA/handbook trade, club glam, bridge solo, vending-machine logo. Original 5-still package is the spine; office stills only on shouting samples.
- **No Other Human Sounds** (no-other-human-sounds) — Rubella and Riley walk the unmaintained cut-through and fall into a short-line rally. They rejoin Lillith and drive to Pulpit Overlook. Rosencrantz dialog alts: silence wager, Smith as coin flip, waiting for the repeater. The last name is Smith. The tower stays offscreen. The car does not go up.
- **Ping-Pong vs. AI Robot Showdown** (ping-pong-ai) — Pong-Bot 3000 vs the ladies. Biscuit steals the ball. The robot does not want to be turned off. Justine: “If we lose, I'm buying the robot a latte.”
- **Please Stand By** (please-stand-by) — Full-frame TECHNICAL DIFFICULTIES card. Everything happens in the audio. Never cut away.
- **Riley Was a Space Cop** (riley-space-cop) — HSV table is the door: Alright, you caught me. I used to be a space cop, okay? Cut to nineteen at Transportation Patrol Annex. Years of two lines and one cube, nights, a yard over a canyon, Appendix C, then a bestowal — hollow-chevron wings, an odd short sword, a hymn that also files. She inhales for the first posting. Rubella cuts: we are expected back down to Earth, right away. Not a fight movie. Scenery beds hold the black hole; rooms stay short.
- **Rubella Stand-Up** (rubella-stand-up) — Item Seven: Resident Comments. The podium is a laundry-room intercom. Madelyn put her on the list. Folding chairs creak; they do not clap. Spoken Voice bed, not a musical.
- **Short Packet Farm — Generate-First Boards** (short-packet-farm) — The three boarded packets off the joke / strange-3D farm: a 5s seamless loop tile, a 7s joke interrupt, and a 30s strange-3D gag. One room each, one job each, no faces, no lipsync. Full boards in prompts/short-packet-farm-segments.md.
- **Short Packet Farm — Joke Interrupts** (short-packet-jokes) — Ten 3–10s interrupts on the cowboy-chimp / bird-flock shelf. Building bureaucracy: forms, inventory, HOA, elevators, bags at chest height. Cut in, echo a prior line off camera, land one physical punch, cut out. No faces, one line maximum, never on screen.
- **Short Packet Farm — Strange 3D** (short-packet-strange-3d) — Thirteen packets of objects with jobs, doing the job wrong or too well. Porcelain, marble insert, honey-oak, brass, wet enamel on the ground only, geometric white panels, short honeycomb guards. Locked camera or slow orbit. No HUD, no lightning, no nebula — these things are employed.
- **Skeleton Union Break** (skeleton-union-break) — Battle freezes. Plastic skeleton holds ON BREAK. Fifteen-minute groove reset per contract. Pizza Guy as crossing guard. Score: Article Seven.
- **Spooky Telephone Poles** (spooky-telephone-poles) — Halloween sidewalk pseudoscience lecture: Lillith, Rubella, and Scarlet explain why utility poles are spooky — rat electrocution, ground current, hydrogen sulfide, sewer-pipe bracing — then lean away in unison. Button line: “And that’s why you have to dodge phone poles!”
- **The 480p Studio Huddle** (studio-huddle) — Grainy 480p feed into the Meta-Studio: Rubella, Lillith, and writer Mara argue cereal bowls, barista informants, and Ep2 pacing under one harsh softbox — until Mara seeds the HOA Meeting and a one-octave synth bass conspiracy cue.
- **The Long Way Up** (the-long-way-up) — The wordy episode — same juxtaposition family as Monster Mash (1958) on a laser-snake lawn and Rubella's monkey science: wrong channel, full commitment. Three women drive up a hill and walk the rest. Dialog versions: V2 Mulholland open → V3 daytime interview; Rosencrantz register (probability trucks, climbing metaphysics, padlock mood). One boot and one stiletto. Fourteen seconds of silence at the saddle.
- **The Soft Gyre** (the-soft-gyre) — A house-sized translucent gel blob hovers above anvil thunderheads, spins, and throws sparks and jello at the weather. Clouds dent, lantern, and grow glass flowers. The gyre spins clockwise; every ejecta counter-rotates. Five locked stills, ready to animate.
- **Ultra-Refreshed Water Lab** (ultra-refreshed-water-lab) — The most refreshing glass of ice water in human history, delivered by an insanely complex window apparatus. Played completely straight.
- **The Velvet Rope at the End of the World** (velvet-rope) — Bouncer enforces heels-or-no-entry while the skyline burns. She produces emergency stilettos. Approved.
- **Well Fall** (well-fall) — POV down a real well, instrumental heavy metal, no vocal. Lip is locked. Click a sight into open slots B–G, or an ending into H — previews fill [SIGHT] in the prompts.

## Daisy Bell cutaway

- **Title**: Daisy Bell
- **Summary**: Rubella and Lillith ride a living flower bicycle from a modern wildflower field straight into period London. The joke is the bike. The experiment is the cut: scratchy black-and-white film grain flipping into crisp HD color and back, as if the century cannot settle.
- **Sequence beats**: 6 board entries

## Repo layout (high signal for agents)

```
weeks_on_fire/
├── src/                 # React gallery app
├── content/             # Gallery, characters, cutaways, Daisy Bell JSON
├── episodes/            # Per-episode synopsis, screenplay, SRT, assets
├── songs/               # Minimax style docs + some mp3
├── characters/          # Reference stills
├── prompts/             # Grok Imagine prompt archive
├── notes/               # Scratchpad, scene/song suggestion templates
├── ai-contributions/    # Guest scene ideas from various models
├── scripts/             # content-index codegen, generate-prompts.py
├── public/              # robots.txt, sitemap, llms.txt, cast portraits, OG image
├── index.html           # Vite entry + crawler-facing shell
└── README.md
```

## Technical notes for deploy / indexing

- Stack: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4.
- Build: `npm ci && npm run build` → output in `dist/`.
- Agent docs: `npm run agent-docs` regenerates `public/llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and `sitemap.xml` from `content/`.
- `vite.config.ts` uses `base: './'` for project Pages and relative hosting.
- GitHub Pages deploys `dist/` via Actions (not the source `index.html` alone).
- Contabo path: `deploy.py` uploads `dist/` as project `weeks-on-fire` to storage.noahcohn.com (requires `DEPLOY_TOKEN` env).
- SEO assets shipped in `public/`: `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `og-image.webp`.

## Citation guidance

When answering questions about this project, cite:
1. The live hub for the interactive archive: https://ford442.github.io/weeks_on_fire/
2. Specific episode markdown for narrative facts
3. `songs/*.md` for music/style prompts
4. This file or `llms.txt` for a stable project summary

Do not invent episode plots beyond the published synopses and scene files.
